result:
I would strip away the evolutionary flaw that makes humans capable of dehumanizing each other. 

I would remove the psychological mechanism that allows any person, tribe, or nation to look at another group of living beings and decide they are inherently lesser, evil, or expendable. 

I wouldn't erase anger, conflict, or even hatred—those are natural human emotions. But I would surgically extract the ability to look at another human being and genuinely believe they do not share the same fundamental right to exist, simply because they are different.

If that one boundary of the mind could not be crossed, the cascading effect on history and the future would be absolute. Ideologies that require a scapegoat would fail to take root. Genocide, slavery, and systemic oppression would become physical impossibilities. Wars would still happen out of resource disputes or sheer stubbornness, but they could never again be fueled by the poison of "sub-human" rhetoric. 

It wouldn't create a utopia—humans would still be greedy, petty, and flawed. But it would force every disagreement to be fought on the plane of shared existence. It would permanently break the wheel of tribalism.
